chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whatever of the foodstuffs you have specified by measuring (kayl), it is not valid to sell by estimation (mujazafah). This is from what is disliked regarding the sale of food.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling food by estimation when it has been specified by measure?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the prohibition of *mujazafah* (sale by estimation) for food items with established standard measures (*kayl*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on eliminating *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions. It underscores the scholarly distinction between fixed measurements and vague estimations, ensuring fairness and preventing disputes in market dealings as practiced during the Imams' era.
